title: Escaped line-break text inside a credential value
description: The text of a credential value contains an escaped line break (backslash and n) in a serialization such as a JSON string, or as plain characters in a log line with no decoder involved.
semantics: Decoding a JSON string turns the escape into a real line feed, which sits inside the decoded value: that inserts a separator, it does not rebuild the credential. In text no decoder reads, the two characters are literal. Whether a consumer decodes and then strips the break is the consumer's behaviour and is not a fact stated here, so the reading is unresolved and the outcome not assertable.

applicability.rationale: Carrier-level: independent of the credential family.

evidenceBasis.rationale: RFC 8259 states which characters must be escaped in a JSON string and that the two-character escape stands for a line feed. Nothing cited says a reader removes it. A maintainer decision would settle it; candidate outcomes are protect the fragments or leave them.

sources.supports: Control characters U+0000 through U+001F must be escaped in a JSON string, and the escape n denotes the line feed U+000A.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
